explanation: Point overrides equals() (line 5) but never overrides hashCode(). HashSet uses hashCode() first to pick a bucket and only calls equals() on objects that land in the same bucket. Since hashCode() falls back to the default identity-based implementation, two Point instances with identical x/y values almost always hash to different buckets, so seen.add(p) never detects them as duplicates even though equals() would say they're the same — hasDuplicate() can silently return false when logical duplicates exist.
prompt: Tap the line that causes this duplicate-detection logic to silently fail.
